analysis.title: ON Holding (ONON): 3Q26 results highlight continued outperformance in a promotional market; TP to $41, remain Buy
key_insights: GS remains Buy on ONON with the 12m price target cut to $41 from $44, implying 9.2% upside from $37.53. The cut comes from a higher risk-free rate (4.5% vs 4.2%) in the DCF, despite higher estimates.
3Q26 net sales were CHF 931.4mn, +17.2% yoy and +17.8% cFX. Adj. EBITDA was CHF 256.8mn.
3Q26 group gross margin was 72.6%, or 66.9% excluding CHF 52.6mn of US tariff refunds, +690bps yoy as reported. GS cites underlying gross margin +320bps yoy.
Adj. EBITDA margin was 27.6% as reported and 21.9% excluding tariff refunds.
3Q26 regional cFX growth: EMEA +19.1%, Americas +12.4%, APAC +31.9%. By channel, DTC +24.8% and Wholesale +13.2%.

Company said US wholesale sell-out improved strongly versus 2Q, and partner inventory levels are healthy. Early signals from the Cloud Surfer 3 launch with run specialty partners were described as exceptional.
The share of online customers under 24 almost doubled yoy, which GS reads as growing traction with younger consumers.
FY26 guidance: net sales growth in the low-20% range cFX, gross margin around 67.5% (66% excluding US tariff refunds), adj. EBITDA margin of 21% to 21.5%.

GS raised FY26E/FY27E cFX sales growth to +21.1%/+17.8% (from +20.3%/+17.8%) and FY26E gross margin to 67.5% (from 65%). Adj. EBITDA margin estimates are 21.3%/21.5% (from 20%/20.6%), with adj. EBITDA of CHF 750mn/895mn (from CHF 700mn/855mn).
GS growth levers into 2027: a refresh of the full running franchise with new superfoams, entry into Football and Golf, continued Sneaker share gains, and scaling apparel from a low base.
Estimate changes: FY26E EPS SFr 1.26 (from 1.13), FY27E 1.39 (from 1.35), FY28E 1.74 (from 1.71). FY26E revenue SFr 3,523.4mn (from 3,502.1mn).
GS FY26E/27E net sales growth is +22bps/-98bps versus Visible Alpha consensus, and adj. EBITDA margin is +118bps/+119bps versus consensus.

Valuation: the $41 DCF target equals c.14.3x 2027E EV/EBITDA (c.20.1x EV/NOPAT). DCF inputs are WACC 11.3%, beta 1.50, terminal growth 3.0%. ONON trades at 23x 12M forward EV/EBITDA versus a 20x-110x range since IPO.

Market backdrop per GS: promotional sportswear market. Key risks include lack of innovation, Vietnam production concentration, FX, a shift in China consumer tastes toward local brands, and a slower DTC mix shift.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $41 from $44 on a higher risk-free rate in the DCF, while FY26E/FY27E estimates were raised after the 3Q26 beat on gross margin and EBITDA margin. Rating stays Buy with 9.2% upside to $37.53.

sector_views.rationale: GS describes the sportswear market as promotional, and ONON as outperforming within it.

ONON 3Q26 reported gross margin 72.6%, or 66.9% excluding CHF 52.6mn of US tariff refunds. Basic EPS reported CHF 0.48 and adj. EPS (basic) CHF 0.53 per GS table, versus CHF 0.36 basic in 3Q25.

GS FY26E estimates: EPS CHF 1.26 (from 1.13), adj. EBITDA CHF 750mn (from 700mn). GS 4Q26E EPS is CHF 0.16 on sales of CHF 909.8mn (+22.3% yoy, +22.6% cFX).

trade_ideas.description: Buy ONON with a 12-month price target of $41
trade_ideas.rationale: GS sees multiple growth levers into 2027 and continued market share gains despite a promotional sportswear market.
trade_ideas.risk: Lack of new innovation, Vietnam supply chain concentration, FX moves, a shift in China consumer tastes to local brands, and a slower DTC mix shift.

risk_factors: A lack of new innovation could hinder ON's ability to maintain premium positioning.
Most production is in Vietnam, which creates supply chain risk.
FX fluctuations could hurt net sales or operating costs.
A shift in China consumer tastes toward local brands could significantly diminish growth prospects.
A slower-than-expected shift in sales mix toward DTC could cause contribution margin downside.
The promotional sportswear market remains an ongoing backdrop.
geopolitical: US tariff refunds boosted ONON's 3Q26 gross margin by CHF 52.6mn.
GS notes the majority of ON's production is based in Vietnam, which exposes it to supply chain risk.
